To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
unconscious emotional expressions elicit corresponding emotional facial reactions.
unconscious exposure to happy faces elicits positive facial muscle reactions, while unconscious exposure to angry faces elicits negative facial muscle reactions.

(1) people spontaneously mimic facial expressions when they are presented with emotional facial expressions and (2) this spontaneous mimicry occurs even when people are not conscious of seeing emotional faces.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the facial reactions to emotional facial expressions that are elicited when the stimuli are consciously perceived also can be elicited when the subjects are prevented from consciously per- ceiving the stimuli.

the question of whether the emotional facial reactions of people are determined by their conscious perception of emotional facial expressions or whether the reactions also can occur on an uncon- scious level.
the study of unconscious emotional processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the unconscious facial reactions are not a result of a mere tendency to mimic, but that they are a result of an automatic and unconscious processing of emotional information.
unconscious emotional reactions can be evoked in response to emotional facial expressions.
the facial reactions to the happy, neutral, or angry faces are not a conscious reaction, but an automatic reaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
emotional expressions can be unconsciously recognized and reacted to, even if the emotional expressions are not perceived consciously.
the human brain has a tendency to automatically mimic emotional expressions.

we have demonstrated that facial EMG re- sponds to emotional stimuli even when the stimuli are presented subliminally, and that these subliminal stimuli can be used to induce emotional responses in the perceiver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emotional facial expressions can trigger corresponding facial reactions even when people are not aware of the facial stimuli.
we have shown that the emotional reactions can occur even when the stimuli were presented at an unconscious level.
emotional expressions have the ability to elicit corresponding facial reactions in a completely unconscious manner.
